items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls; it can only use text in the current window. If the program does not re-send the earlier exchange, the model has no access to it. Options a, c and d assume hidden memory that does not exist, which is the misconception that agents remember automatically (M3).
Call 2 sends 900 + 50 (request) + 350 (result) = 1300. Call 3 sends 1300 + 50 + 350 = 1700, since each call re-sends the full history. An answer of 350 or 400 treats only the newest text as sent.

Memory between sessions is storage the program writes and loads into the next window. A large window (a) does not survive the session ending, the model has no memory to ask (c), and a manual search (d) would not hold a student's personal status.

The model reads only the chunks the search returns, so the answer quality is capped by retrieval quality. The model never read the whole manual (a), a larger window would not bring the missing chunk in (b), and no earlier chats are involved (d).

items.answer: Whole transcripts are large and would fill the context window, costing tokens on every call and hurting recall; save small facts instead.
accepted: It would use up too many tokens and clutter the window, so save short facts rather than full chats.
Loading everything costs a lot on every call and makes the model less accurate; only the relevant facts should be loaded.
Too expensive and fills the context; save only key facts like training status.
items.rationale: Any one valid reason is full credit: cost grows because everything loaded is re-sent at every step, the window has a limit, recall declines as it fills (context rot), and most transcript text is irrelevant. Saying it is poor only for privacy, with no link to context, is partial.
